newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU urges easterns to adopt its standards.
newsitem.headline: EU urges easterns to adopt its standards.

text.p: The European Union underlined on Thursday that eastern European countries must bring their goods like pharmaceutical products, food and vehicles into line with EU standards on health and safety as part of their process of accession.
At a meeting of the Internal Market Council the European Commission said it wanted to approach the issue in the same way it was doing with candidate Poland.

Poland is working towards the progressive alignment to the "acquis communautaire" according to an agreed calendar and on this basis a system of European conformity assessment agreements is being set up.
In return, the EU agrees measures to help the trade in the products which fulfil the EU requirements and provides technical assistance and cooperation.

The Commission said in a document made available to the ministerial meeting it would seek confirmation of these four elements from other candidate countries in the framework of the association agreements they hold with the EU.
It said a calendar for progressive alignment to the acquis communautaire would need to be established by the candidate ocuntries.
It said that conformity agreements should be seen only as an intermediate step, designed not only to facilitate trade, but at the same time to support the alignment process.
